figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview of the proposed muscle fatigue detection framework. a. Personalized SNN pipeline with feature extraction, spike encoding, SNN inference, and QAF post-processing. b. The three components of our robustness enhancement method, SDH. c. Low-bit weight quantization from FP32 to signed integers.
Fig. 2. CU design and associated scheduler.

Fig. 4. Comparison of differential features and all features. a. Spectral entropy mean values of scaled EMG show significant differences in fatigue and nonfatigue muscle. b. WAMP mean values of scaled EMG show non-significant differences in fatigue and non-fatigue muscle. c. Comparison of F1 score from 30 users. d. Comparison of F1 score by features setting. All shaded areas represent the 95% confidence interval of the measurements from 30 users.

Fig. 5. Ablation study on timestep and energy analysis. a, d Performance variation with timesteps from 2 to 24 for the SUE and SPE datasets, respectively. b, e Averaged F1-scores with standard deviation, highlighting the optimal timesteps (T=15 for SUE and T=6 for SPE). c, f Energy costs comparisons between the baseline MLP and our spike-based models. Spike rates are collected and shown for each model.
